= List continuation and topology

== Repeated description-list continuations

[horizontal]
Owner:: Principal description text.
+
An attached paragraph owned by Owner.
+
NOTE: An attached admonition owned by Owner.
+
[source,rust]
----
fn owned() {
    println!("owner");
}
----
Sibling:: This sibling remains a separate row.

== Nested description lists

Root one:: Root one description.
Child one::: Child one description.
Grandchild one:::: Grandchild one description.
Child two::: Child two description.
Root two:: Root two description.

Protocols::
HTTP::: Transfers web resources.
Headers:::: Carry request metadata.
SSH::: Provides a secure shell.

Final:: A root sibling after the nested topology.

== Delimiter transitions

.Shorter second delimiter
First deep term::: First deep description.
Root term:: Root description.

.Skipped delimiter depth
Root jump:: Root jump description.
Deep jump:::: Deep jump description.

.Semicolon to colon
Semicolon term;; Semicolon description.
Colon child:: Colon child description.

.Colon to semicolon
Colon term:: Colon description.
Semicolon child;; Semicolon child description.

== Formatted terms

[qanda]
What has *strong* and _emphasized_ words?:: The mixed term preserves both formats.
*Whole strong question?*:: A whole-term format.
What contains `code` and https://example.com[a link]?:: Code and link formats.

== Titled list boundaries

[qanda]
First list question?:: First list answer.

.Second list title
[qanda]
Second list question?:: Second list answer.

.Plain description-list title
Plain term:: Plain definition.

== Effective marker styles

[style=ordered]
Named ordered:: Named style is effective.

[style=unordered]
Named unordered:: Named style is effective.

== Continued mixed lists

* Outer unordered owner
+
--
. First ordered child
. Second ordered child
** Unordered grandchild under the second ordered child
** Second unordered grandchild
--
* Following unordered sibling

. Outer ordered owner
+
--
* First unordered child
* Second unordered child
.. Ordered grandchild under the second unordered child
.. Second ordered grandchild
--
. Following ordered sibling

Answered question?:: This question has an answer.
